standard_prerequisites.name: Cohomology of a sheaf on a ringed site via an injective resolution
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard in this chapter: H^n(U, F) is computed as the cohomology of the complex of sections of an injective resolution, and the restriction map is induced by restricting representatives
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the presentation of H^n(U, F) displayed in the proof and the compatibility of restriction with the representative; the covering argument itself is the counted content.

standard_prerequisites.name: An injective resolution is exact in positive degrees
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Standard: for n > 0 the sheafified cohomology of the complex I^bullet vanishes, so Im(I^{n-1} -> I^n) = Ker(I^n -> I^{n+1})
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the identification of image and kernel sheaves used to produce the local primitives; locating those primitives on a covering is inside the counted proof.

core_obligations: Present the class: choose an injective resolution F -> I^bullet and use the displayed description of H^n(U, F) as Ker(I^n(U) -> I^{n+1}(U)) modulo Im(I^{n-1}(U) -> I^n(U)) to pick a representative tilde xi in I^n(U) of the given class xi (proof lines 725-733).

Find local primitives: because I^bullet is exact in degree n and tilde xi is a section of the kernel sheaf over U, there is a covering {U_i -> U} of the site such that each restricted section tilde xi|_{U_i} lies in the image of the differential d from I^{n-1}(U_i) (proof lines 733-741).

Conclude: by the definition of the restriction of a cohomology class as the class of the restricted representative, each xi|_{U_i} vanishes on the covering, which is the assertion for n > 0 (proof lines 741-743).
proof_roadmap: Write the cohomology group of U as the cohomology of the complex of sections of an injective resolution and choose a representative of the class (proof lines 725-733).
Since the resolution is exact in degree n, the image sheaf of d equals the kernel sheaf, so the representative is locally in the image of d on a covering (proof lines 733-741).
Translate the local primitives back through the definition of restriction to conclude that the class dies on the covering (proof lines 741-743).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a sheaf F of O-modules on a ringed site, an object U, an integer n > 0 and a cohomology class xi in H^n(U, F), some covering {U_i -> U} of the site restricts xi to zero on every U_i (statement lines 716-721). The point that cannot be done by pure formalism is the passage from the class to a representative and from the representative to local primitives: the injective resolution must be used in two ways at once, first to present H^n(U, F) as a quotient of sections of I^n(U) and then, using exactness of the resolution in degree n, to know that the image sheaf of the differential equals the kernel sheaf, which is exactly what produces a covering over which the representative is a coboundary (proof lines 725-741). The class is then killed because restriction of a cohomology class is represented by the restricted section. The claim is H2: short, no citation, but with a genuine two-step use of the resolution.
